summary: Oxford County, Maine lookout from 1910, steel tower by 1919; the register says it was removed in 2004, and no source describes the site since.

facts.design: Steel tower, 24 feet, per the 1920 inventory
facts.status_note: Removed in 2004 according to the register; no source describes the site since then

events.note: Established with a wood tower (Maine Historical Society photo inventory)
Home camp for the watchman built; a lookout cabin being moved to the summit, with the foreman's completion not yet reported (1917 report)
New steel tower erected on the moved site; the 1919 annual report and 1920 inventory give 24 feet, a 1919 district report about 27, and a Kennebec item 36
Register says removed in 2004; no other source read gives a removal date
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: 27 ft (1919 district report), 36 ft (Daily Kennebec Journal, 1919, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page), 24 ft (1919 annual report and 1920 inventory). Facts use 24 ft, the figure matching the brief's 7.3 m. Location conflict: Lincoln Plantation (district report, register) vs Grafton (Kennebec item). Maine Memory dating conflict: title ca. 1929, creation date circa 1920. The 2004 removal rests on the register alone. No source found describing the site today or public access. Brief record otherwise consistent: gone, FFLOS US 84, registered 2008, agency Maine Forestry District.
